glosses: Accustomed to human contact.
Docile or tranquil towards humans.

examples.text: The lion was quite tame.

glosses: Of a person, well-behaved; not radical or extreme.

examples.text: What, for example, were Fraunhofer's lines? McArdle had just been studying the matter with the aid of our tame scientist at the office, and he picked from his desk two of those many-coloured spectral bands which bear a general resemblance to the hat-ribbons of some young and ambitious cricket club.

glosses: Of a non-Westernised person, accustomed to European society.

examples.text: The victim was Captain Bickenson, who had gone there from Port Darwin to try the pearling grounds, and for this purpose employed a number of tame blacks about the schooner.

glosses: Not exciting.

examples.text: This party is too tame for me.
For a thriller, that film was really tame.

Wow! So the implication there is that even 12-year-olds in France will find the movie tame. “Yes, eet was a, an amusing erotic trifle, I supposa. Ze love-making was passable, but, uh, belt play is a leettle pedestriahn, don’t you seenk?”.

glosses: Crushed; subdued; depressed; spiritless.

examples.text: tame slaves of the laborious plough

glosses: Capable of being represented as a finite closed polygonal chain.
To make (an animal) tame; to domesticate.

examples.text: He tamed the wild horse.

Richard Wrangham has noted that the domestication of animals usually tames them by slowing down components of the developmental timetable to retain juvenile traits into adulthood, a process called pedomorphy or neoteny.
Due to his ingenuity Homo learned to unleash the energy of wood by taming wild fire and stepped into the pyrocultural age.

glosses: To make submissive or docile.

examples.text: The governor tames the engine.

glosses: To take control of something that is unruly.

examples.text: Police have to tame the riots.

glosses: To become tame or domesticated.

examples.text: Tambourines are shy birds and do not tame easily.

glosses: To make gentle or meek.

examples.text: Guard dogs need to be tamed so that they know who not to attack.

None but Adrian could have tamed the motley population of London, which, like a troop of unbitted steeds rushing to their pastures, had thrown aside all minor fears, through the operation of the fear paramount.

glosses: To broach or enter upon; to taste, as a liquor; to divide; to distribute; to deal out.

examples.text: In the time of famine he is the Joseph of the country, and keeps the poor from starving. Then he tameth his stacks of corn, which not his covetousness, but providence, hath reserved for time of need.

glosses: Rendre un animal moins sauvage.

examples.text: Le petit prince a apprivoisé le renard.

glosses: Faire d’un animal sauvage un animal privé.

examples.text: Le coq de Sonnerat est plein de courage et de résolution; aussi est-il très estimé dans l’Indoustan comme oiseau de combat. Les vrais amateurs indiens ne se servent pas de coqs élevés à l'état domestique, mais bien de sujets sauvages, que du reste ils apprivoisent en assez peu de temps; […].

glosses: Rendre quelqu’un plus doux, plus traitable.

examples.text: Apprivoiser un sauvage.
C’était un homme peu sociable, on a eu bien de la peine à l’apprivoiser.
La fille demeura. Tout doucement il vous l’apprivoisa ; Lui prit d’abord son joli bras d’ivoire; Puis s’approcha, puis en vint au baiser
Ce sont des gens très conservateurs. Il faudra les apprivoiser.

glosses: Rendre familier.

examples.text: La mécanique d’Akropolis, possible As d’or au festival de Cannes la semaine prochaine, est plutôt simple, mais elle s’apprivoise.

glosses: Devenir moins sauvage (animal).

examples.text: Les loups s’apprivoisent facilement.

glosses: Devenir plus doux, plus sociable, s’accoutumer, s’habituer (personne).

examples.text: Cet enfant était bien farouche, il s’est apprivoisé peu à peu à notre contact.

glosses: S’accoutumer à la vue du danger, à l’exemple du vice.

examples.text: S’apprivoiser avec le danger, avec le vice,
C’est donc ainsi qu’insensiblement on avance vers le précipice ; …] on s’apprivoise avec le danger, on commence à n’en avoir plus tant de peur, […].
